statement: Binning quantizers preserve policy smoothness better than learned quantizers; deterministic experts more often violate RTVC.
source: arXiv:2603.20538, Section 4.1 (empirical claim; no released dataset/code)

mutation_test.name: increase expert stochasticity (sigma 0.3 -> 2.0)
mutation_test.effect: More stochasticity smooths the quantized-policy distribution, so RTVC violations drop (0.2107 -> 0.0000), confirming the test is sensitive to the determinism/smoothness structure the claim depends on.

notes: TOY / synthetic. The paper gives no released experiment for this claim; we reproduce the qualitative phenomenon with a controlled synthetic setup. RTVC violation rates: binning_det=0.1482, learned_det=0.2107 (learned>binning: True); binning_sto=0.0000, learned_sto=0.0000 (det>sto: True). The ordering matches the claim's direction where the synthetic setup resolves it; full verification would require the paper's (unreleased) empirical data.
